ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, let there be an equilateral triangle $ABC$ with side length $a$. Let $P$ be a point on side $AB$, and draw $PE\perp AC$ at point $E$. Let $Q$ be a point on the extension of $BC$. When $AP=CQ$, line $PQ$ intersects $AC$ at point $D$. What is the length of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, extend line $AD$ through point $Q$ and draw a perpendicular line to it at point $F$, \\
since $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, \\
therefore $\angle A=\angle ACB=60^\circ$, \\
since $\angle ACB=\angle QCF$, \\
therefore $\angle QCF=\angle A=60^\circ$, \\
also, since $PE\perp AC$, $QF\perp AC$, \\
therefore $\angle AEP=\angle CFQ=90^\circ$, \\
and $AP=CQ$, \\
therefore $\triangle AEP\cong \triangle CFQ$ (AAS), \\
therefore $AE=CF$, $PE=QF$, \\
Similarly, it can be proved that $\triangle DEP\cong \triangle DFQ$, \\
therefore $DE=DF$, \\
therefore $AC=AE+DE+CD=DE+CD+CF=DE+DF=2DE$, \\
therefore $DE=\frac{1}{2}AC=\frac{1}{2}a$. \\
Hence, $DE=\boxed{\frac{1}{2}a}$.

method.method_draft: Use Menelaus plus a right-triangle projection. From the figure, note that P lies on AB, Q lies on the extension of BC beyond C, and the straight line PQ meets AC at D; E is the foot from P to AC. Let AP=CQ=x. Then PB=a-x and BQ=BC+CQ=a+x. Apply Menelaus in triangle ABC to the transversal P-D-Q: (AP/PB)(BQ/QC)(CD/DA)=1. This gives (x/(a-x))((a+x)/x)(CD/DA)=1, so CD/DA=(a-x)/(a+x). Since AD+CD=a, solve AD=(a+x)/2. method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是三角形 ABC，A 在上方，B 在左下方，C 在下方偏右，BC 向右延长到 Q。点 P 在边 AB 上，线段 PE 从 P 作到边 AC，并在 E 处有直角标记，表示 PE 垂直 AC。直线 PQ 从 P 向右下方经过 AC 上的 D，再延伸到 Q。因此 P、D、Q 共线，D、E 都在 AC 上，且 E 比 D 更靠近 A。

推理：设 AP=CQ=x。因为 ABC 是边长为 a 的等边三角形，所以 AB=BC=AC=a。于是 PB=AB-AP=a-x，且 Q 在 BC 的延长线上，所以 BQ=BC+CQ=a+x。对三角形 ABC 中的截线 P-D-Q 使用梅涅劳斯定理：
(AP/PB)(BQ/QC)(CD/DA)=1。
代入 AP=x，PB=a-x，BQ=a+x，QC=x，得
(x/(a-x))((a+x)/x)(CD/DA)=1，
所以 CD/DA=(a-x)/(a+x)。又 AD+CD=AC=a，因此
AD = (a+x)/2。
因为 ABC 为等边三角形，∠PAC=60°；又 PE⊥AC，所以在直角三角形 AEP 中，AP 是斜边，AE=AP·cos60°=x/2。由图中 E、D 在 AC 上且 D 比 E 更靠近 C，可得
DE=AD-AE=(a+x)/2-x/2=a/2。

Put A=(0,0), C=(a,0), and because ABC is equilateral with B on the opposite side of AC from Q, take B=(a/2,-sqrt(3)a/2). Let AP=CQ=x. raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, let there be an equilateral triangle $ABC$ with side length $a$. Let $P$ be a point on side $AB$, and draw $PE\perp AC$ at point $E$. Let $Q$ be a point on the extension of $BC$. When $AP=CQ$, line $PQ$ intersects $AC$ at point $D$. What is the length of $DE$?
raw_record.answer: Solution: Extend line $AD$ through point $Q$ and draw a perpendicular line to it at point $F$. Since $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, $\angle A=\angle ACB=60^\circ$. Since $\angle ACB=\angle QCF$, therefore $\angle QCF=\angle A=60^\circ$. Also, since $PE\perp AC$ and $QF\perp AC$, $\angle AEP=\angle CFQ=90^\circ$. And $AP=CQ$, therefore $\triangle AEP\cong \triangle CFQ$ (AAS), so $AE=CF$, $PE=QF$. Similarly, it can be proved that $\triangle DEP\cong \triangle DFQ$, therefore $DE=DF$. Then $AC=AE+DE+CD=DE+CD+CF=DE+DF=2DE$, so $DE=\frac{1}{2}AC=\frac{1}{2}a$. Hence, $DE=\boxed{\frac{1}{2}a}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is below and slightly to the right, and BC is extended rightward to Q. Point P is on side AB, segment PE is drawn from P to side AC, and there is a right-angle mark at E, indicating that PE is perpendicular to AC. Line PQ goes from P toward the lower right through D on AC, then extends to Q. Therefore P, D, Q are collinear, D and E are both on AC, and E is closer to A than D.

Reasoning: Let AP=CQ=x. Because ABC is an equilateral triangle with side length a, AB=BC=AC=a. Thus PB=AB-AP=a-x, and Q is on the extension of BC, so BQ=BC+CQ=a+x. Use Menelaus' theorem for the secant P-D-Q in triangle ABC:
(AP/PB)(BQ/QC)(CD/DA)=1.
Substituting AP=x, PB=a-x, BQ=a+x, QC=x, gives
(x/(a-x))((a+x)/x)(CD/DA)=1,
so CD/DA=(a-x)/(a+x). Also AD+CD=AC=a, therefore
AD = (a+x)/2.
Because ABC is an equilateral triangle, ∠PAC=60°; also PE⊥AC, so in right triangle AEP, AP is the hypotenuse, AE=AP·cos60°=x/2. From the figure, E and D are on AC and D is closer to C than E, so
DE=AD-AE=(a+x)/2-x/2=a/2.
